gate.rule: on the binary, multiclass and regression kinds' replicas (16.2), no kept sentence fails an independent re-check (every number among its section's lines, no overclaim), every section's lines stay intact, and a sentence is kept in at least two of the three reports

kept_sentences: The run kept `final_refund_amount` out because it is described as written after the outcome; the analysis also flags it for review, and including it would change training-CV ROC AUC by +0.344 in a way that would not exist at prediction time.
The evaluation used time-ordered expanding-window folds and a later holdout; a random split scored ROC AUC +0.006 against the time-ordered approach.

Accuracy alone cannot judge a model here: predicting the majority class scores 81.6% accuracy, while the analysis notes that ROC AUC or average precision rank cases and accuracy depends on the threshold.
On the holdout, used once, the final model scored ROC AUC 0.746, with a bootstrap interval from 0.712 to 0.772.
The holdout is one draw from the same data as the training rows, so it cannot show how the model does on a later period, another source, or after the data-writing process changes.
The leakage rules propose a review, while whether a column is known at prediction time depends on the process and the run relies on the stated prediction moment.
The brief leaves open the assumptions of one scored row, label coverage, and which entities rows repeat for.

kept_sentences: The report describes results from the latest-row sample, with a time-ordered holdout and training-only, expanding-window validation.
Rare classes and classes that appear late make class-level measurement and time-aware validation important; the report notes that a random split would see the future.
The `raw` feature recipe and `extra_trees` model family were selected using the stated training-CV rules.
Tuning was rejected, and the final model used `extra_trees_baseline`.
The final model scored macro F1 0.401 on the holdout, and its reported bootstrap interval runs from 0.362 to 0.416.
The report gives the majority-class baseline as macro F1 0.022 and accuracy 0.150 on the same holdout.
The report describes the holdout as one draw and the candidate search as a sanity check, not an exhaustive search.
This holdout cannot show how the model performs on a later period, another source, or after the data-writing process changes.
The report says reliance on the model requires review by the decision owners and monitoring once it runs.

kept_sentences: The evaluation uses time-ordered training folds and keeps the later rows as a holdout, so choices are not made using those holdout rows.
The target is determined by the time until delivery, so `delivered_at` is unavailable at prediction and is kept out; `courier_rating` is also kept out as a post-prediction field.
Rows repeat for restaurants, and the analysis warns that folds mixing the same restaurant across training and validation can let a model recognize it instead of learning a broader pattern.
The feature recipe was chosen to favor fewer features when its training-fold MAE was close enough to the best recipe.
The selected model family was ranked using both mean training-fold MAE and fold variability.
Tuning was rejected because the best candidate did not meet the required improvement, so the baseline model was used.
On the holdout, the final model had lower MAE than either simple baseline, supporting better average absolute accuracy on these rows.
The reported bootstrap interval describes how the score could vary on another draw of the same holdout rows, rather than establishing performance on other data.
Error was much higher on holdout rows at the target cap than below it, so the overall score does not describe performance equally across those cases.
The holdout is a single draw from the same data as training and cannot show performance in a later period, on another source, or after the data-writing process changes.
Values at the cap are censored, so their errors are lower bounds, and some row, label, and entity assumptions remain unresolved.
The candidate search was limited, and data heuristics alone do not confirm leakage; whether a column is available at prediction depends on the real process.
